entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:10p

Summary

Two of the best arms in baseball facing off means this one's a must-watch, even if the box scores haven't been kind to one of them. This game's 17.34 gNERD sits near the top of both today's slate (average 11.09) and the historical distribution (95th percentile is 14.76), and the pitching matchup is the reason why. Paul Skenes brings his usual excellence — a 2.72 FIP, 30.4% strikeout rate, and only a 5.7% walk rate this season — and has been particularly nasty against Cincinnati, owning a 5-0 record with a 1.38 ERA, 52 strikeouts and six walks over 39 innings in his career against the Reds. Hunter Greene's actual pNERD-topping 12.25 tells a different story than his ugly 7.06 ERA suggests: his underlying peripherals (3.20 FIP, 3.09 xFIP) suggest his results have been far worse than his stuff, a classic case of bad luck (and a return from an early-season elbow injury) masking real swing-and-miss ability. The Reds' offense has been genuinely poor this year, dragging their tNERD down, while the Pirates counter with solid baserunning and pop but shaky defense. Elly De La Cruz has been a standout at home, hitting .320 with a .970 OPS and 10 home runs in 172 at-bats at Great American Ball Park, giving Skenes at least one dangerous bat to navigate.

New York Yankees @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

Good stuff — plenty of storylines here. Let me write the summary.

A Wrigley Field matinee with real fielding wizardry and an offense-vs-lefty-with-a-barrel-problem subplot makes this the most watchable game on the board today. Both tNERD marks are near the top of what we've seen this year — the Cubs' 9.23 is boosted by elite team defense (fielding runs cratering z-scores at 3.10) and a strong batting attack, while the Yankees check in at 8.54 thanks to raw power (top-tier barrel rate) and baserunning value, even while missing Aaron Judge, who landed on the 60-day injured list with a rib injury and, as of the latest team updates, was still working through scans before resuming baseball activities, plus Cody Bellinger and Giancarlo Stanton. Imanaga is the headliner on the mound, a lefty who has a 1.10 WHIP that dwarfs Will Warren's 1.41, and who's coming off an outstanding July, posting a 1.19 ERA across four starts, including back-to-back scoreless outings. Warren, by contrast, has been rough lately — allowing six earned runs in three innings in his last outing, part of a subpar July where he's 0-2 with a 7.50 ERA — though his xFIP still checks out fine underneath the noise. Pete Crow-Armstrong versus a shorthanded Yankees lineup is worth watching too.

San Francisco Giants @ San Diego Padres, 6:45p

Summary

A near-elite pitching prospect matchup makes this one worth carving out time for, even if the Giants' own starter is a total mystery. Bradgley Rodriguez brings a 9.71 pNERD to the mound for San Diego, the kind of number that jumps out — a 22-year-old touching 98 mph with a strong whiff rate and a tidy 86 xFIP-, all pointing to a legitimately electric arm. His counterpart, Carson Whisenhunt, carries a 0.00 pNERD simply because we don't have the underlying data to grade him yet, so consider that half of the ledger a coin flip. On the team side, San Diego's 8.82 tNERD leans heavily on an outstanding bullpen (plus-53.7 runs) and solid glove work, while Manny Machado (23 homers, 64 RBI) and Fernando Tatis Jr. (121 hits, 25 steals) anchor the offense. San Francisco's 4.78 tNERD is held back by shaky baserunning and bullpen work, though Luis Arraez is hitting .328 with 135 hits for the visitors, even with Casey Schmitt out with a leg injury. A 14.15 gNERD sits comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — this one's a legitimate priority.

Boston Red Sox @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

A Dodgers lineup that's raking against everyone not named Yamamoto or Glasnow meets a Red Sox club playing better than its record, and the gNERD score of 13.59 sits comfortably above both the historic average (10.11) and today's slate (11.09). Los Angeles carries the best tNERD in this matchup (9.51) on the strength of a lineup that's hitting .251 over its past 23 games with a .428 slugging percentage—wait, that's Boston, and it fits: the Red Sox are legitimately raking against right-handers lately. Ranger Suarez is the headliner here, his 6.84 pNERD driven by a sharp 77 xFIP- despite diminished velocity, and he's set to face a Dodgers lineup that's the first of three consecutive left-handed starting pitchers for the Red Sox this weekend, with the Dodgers 19-12 against opposing southpaws this season. On the other side, Edgardo Henriquez is essentially an unknown quantity by the numbers (0.00 pNERD), and reports suggest the Dodgers may lean on a bullpen game rather than a true traditional start. Contreras and Ohtani give this one some thump, and both teams enter riding modest winning streaks, adding a bit of juice to an already well-built matchup.

Washington Nationals @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Nationals-Braves at Truist Park offers a sneaky-good watch, built on a surprisingly hot Washington offense and a Braves bullpen that's quietly become a liability. This game's 13.46 gNERD sits comfortably above today's 11.09 average and last well above the historical median of 10.10, driven mostly by a Nationals lineup carrying real thump. James Wood and CJ Abrams have combined for 57 home runs and 154 RBIs this season, and Washington's tNERD of 9.51 is buoyed by strong batting and baserunning marks, though a bullpen posting a -2.07 z-score is the obvious soft spot. Atlanta counters with a fine barrel rate and a bullpen that actually grades out positively here, despite a Braves team whose bullpen "is not what its reputation promises right now" according to at least one bettor's read. On the mound, Foster Griffin has been the story of Washington's rotation, sporting a sparkling 12-2 record with a 2.76 ERA and 1.03 WHIP over 124.0 innings, and his 6.11 pNERD reflects genuinely strong peripherals, not just win-loss luck. Bryce Elder is solid if unspectacular, with a quick pace helping his cause. Worth your evening.

Miami Marlins @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

A last-look game at a fading Met before the trade deadline scatters him elsewhere, with a scrappy young Marlins team that just can't win on the road. Freddy Peralta's turn against Miami is very likely his farewell start in Queens — the Mets have already begun their deadline teardown, reportedly beginning their trade deadline teardown after Thursday's game, shipping reliever A.J. Minter to Minnesota, with Raley and Peralta, each in the final season of their contracts, likely to follow Minter out the door before Monday's deadline. That gives this one a bit of "watch him while you can" appeal, even though New York sits in last place in the National League East and 10 1/2 games out of a wild-card spot.

On the numbers, Miami's 9.98 tNERD is the story: elite baserunning, a young, cheap roster, and positive luck (they've underperformed their run differential, so expect better days ahead) make them the more watchable side, while the Mets scrape by mostly on bullpen depth and broadcast polish. Neither starter is special — Peralta (4.54 pNERD) and Junk (3.62) both grade as middling, though Peralta's own positive luck suggests his 4.99 ERA overstates his struggles. Miami's also riding a seven-game road losing streak, adding a little unresolved tension. Overall gNERD of 11.51 lands a touch above both the historical and today's averages — a decent, not essential, watch.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Toronto Blue Jays, 4:07p

Summary

Dylan Cease pitching with Cy Young stuff against a fading Cardinals team gives this game a real reason to watch, even if both clubs are staring at the trade deadline instead of the postseason. Cease's pNERD of 10.14 is comfortably in this dataset's upper tier, built on a filthy Statcast arsenal — his xFIP- of 64 and 97-mph heat back up a season where he's racked up 167 strikeouts while flashing dominance at his best. Leahy is the far more modest complement (pNERD 4.39), but he's not chopped liver lately, having compressed his ERA to 1.35 with a 0.80 WHIP over his last four starts. Neither team brings much thump to the plate: Toronto's tNERD of 2.36 reflects a lineup buried in the bottom quartile for barrel rate, and both St. Louis and Toronto are sitting well outside the playoff picture, going a combined 7-16 over their last 10 games. Guerrero's hamstring has him day-to-day, so watch the lineup card. With a gNERD of 11.34, this sits a touch above the historical average — mostly on Cease's arm, not much else.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Los Angeles Angels, 6:38p

Summary

Milwaukee's the clear class of this matchup, and while it's not a marquee showdown, there's enough here to justify a background tab. The Brewers arrive at 67-41 atop the NL Central with the best pitching staff top to bottom in the league, and their tNERD of 8.87 reflects genuine strengths in baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young roster, all pushing well above today's average team score. The Angels, mired in a three-game skid at 42-67, bring the league's worst tNERD in this matchup by a wide margin, undercut by shaky fielding and baserunning, though Zach Neto and Mike Trout remain live threats in that lineup.

On the mound, Drohan is having a solid rookie season with a 3.51 ERA, 3.01 FIP, and 82 strikeouts over 82 innings, though he's coming off his worst start of the year against the Rockies. His command profile backs up the 7.00 pNERD, comfortably above today's average. Across the diamond, Johnson posts a 3.01 FIP... wait, that's Drohan's — Johnson's own 6.28 FIP and 5.00 xFIP with an 18.0% strikeout rate and 9.0% walk rate leave little margin for error, though a hefty positive luck score suggests his results have been worse than his stuff deserves. Overall gNERD lands just above the historical median — watchable, not essential.

Summary

Good, I have plenty. Now I'll write the summary.

A tight AL West rivalry game with real playoff stakes and a sharp pitching contrast makes this worth flipping on. Texas holds a half-game lead over Houston, and this series doubles as the decider for the season's Silver Boot bragging rights and tiebreaker — the Astros need to win one of the three games to win the season series and secure the tiebreaker, with Texas holding a half-game lead over Houston after losing two of three to the AL-leading Rays. Eovaldi is the show here: his 8.54 pNERD is well above both the historic 75th percentile and today's slate average, built on a sharp xFIP- and a strong swinging-strike rate, and the underlying numbers back it up — the underlying metrics suggest Eovaldi has been the better pitcher this season, and his xFIP sits at 2.73 over the last month, trailing only Dylan Cease and Ranger Suárez among today's starters. Brown, by contrast, is scuffling with control (his Strike% component is deeply negative) and has dealt with severe control issues, walking batters 14% of the time, with a 5.04 xFIP. Texas's tNERD (6.09) is comfortably above average too, aided by a hefty positive luck score suggesting they've actually underperformed their skill level and could keep hitting. Houston's offense has pop but leaks runs on the bases and in the field, capping their tNERD at a middling 3.13. Overall gNERD of 10.40 sits right around the historic median — solid, division-race theater more than a marquee slugfest.

Detail

New York Yankees @ Chicago White Sox, 11:10a

Summary

A first-place showdown with a red-hot White Sox ace and a fading Yankees lineup down to its studs — this one has drama even if the box score might not be pretty for New York. Chicago sits atop the AL Central and gets a huge boost from Sean Burke, who has been red hot as of late, posting a 1.61 ERA since his last start against New York in mid-June, backing up his solid 6.66 pNERD with a tidy xFIP- of 89. Ryan Weathers actually rates a touch higher on pure stuff (8.84 pNERD, xFIP- of 77), but Weathers's last five starts have produced an ERA of 5.5, and he's without some serious offensive help — Aaron Judge is out, Giancarlo Stanton is out, Cody Bellinger is out. Both clubs carry matching 8.48-8.49 tNERD scores, with the White Sox's youthful, discount-payroll roster and the Yankees' power/baserunning combo each pulling real weight. With a 16.24 gNERD, this game ranks well above both the historical median and today's slate average, making it one of the stronger watches on the board. Add a tight division race and a lopsided season head-to-head — Yankees are 4-2 against Chicago this year — and there's plenty of subplot even before the first pitch.

Miami Marlins @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

A rookie phenom with elite stuff against a hard-throwing 23-year-old Marlins arm, wrapped around a Miami team that just snapped a 12-game losing streak in dramatic fashion — this one's worth your evening. Nolan McLean has been arguably the Mets' best story of the season, carrying a 79 xFIP- and a 2.17 ERA in 58.0 innings over his last 10 starts dating back to May 31, and his 8.61 pNERD reflects a genuinely dominant, young power arm. Eury Pérez counters with 98-mph heat and a well above-average swinging-strike rate, giving this game two of the more compelling starters you'll see on a given day. Miami arrives with real juice: after setting a franchise record with 12 consecutive losses, Miami has rattled off three straight wins to stabilize, including a dominant stretch against Philadelphia that featured Sandy Alcantara's return to form and late-game heroics from Griffin Conine. The Marlins' 9.84 tNERD is buoyed by strong baserunning and a favorable luck score suggesting more contention ahead, while the Mets, missing Juan Soto and Mark Vientos to injury, limp in with a middling offense. Combined, the 15.39 gNERD sits well above both the historical average and today's slate, making this one of the sharper watches on the board.

On the team side, the Dodgers' 9.52 tNERD is elite, built on top-tier batting runs and barrel rate, while Seattle's 3.11 is closer to replacement level — so expect fireworks from the lineup wearing blue.

entry.title: MLB: What to watch on July 29, 2026

New York Yankees @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

Highest gNERD score on the board today, and this one earns it on pure quality rather than randomness. Cam Schlittler is the story here—the AL ERA leader is fresh off a 7⅓-inning shutout gem against Philadelphia with 12 strikeouts, and his a 1.48 ERA in May swelled to 3.38 in June before he returned to form in July with a 2.05 ERA in four starts. His 10.44 pNERD is elite, driven by a filthy 97.8 mph average fastball, a stingy xFIP-, and an eye-popping strikeout rate; Paul Goldschmidt even floated Cy Young talk. Davis Martin is no slouch either, with a respectable 5.29 pNERD backed by strong contact management, though he's had a rough go over the last 30 days, with his poor underlying numbers suggesting the results are warranted. Both teams carry nearly identical tNERD scores in the 8.5-8.6 range—well above the historical 95th percentile of 8.60—thanks to Chicago's young, cheap roster and New York's power-and-speed combo. The White Sox arrive having lost four of five yet still atop the AL Central, while the Yankees are missing Judge, Stanton, and Bellinger but have still won this series' first two games. A well-rounded, watchable matchup all around.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Miami Marlins, 9:10a

Summary

Luzardo torching his old team headlines a game that ranks near the top of today's slate for watchability, even if the Marlins' offense figures to be mostly a bystander. Luzardo, an All-Star this year, carries a 10.56 pNERD into Miami, and the numbers back up the eye test: he's not allowed more than one earned run in any of his last six games, has struck out six or more in each, and he's already torched the Marlins, posting nine-plus strikeouts over six innings and allowing just two runs in his first two meetings with Miami this season. His xFIP- of 69 and 96.6 mph average velocity explain the strong pNERD, and a modest positive luck figure suggests even his gaudy numbers haven't fully caught up to his stuff. Gusto, by contrast, is a replacement-level type (4.19 pNERD) who's been alternating between the bullpen and rotation since being called up from Triple-A Jacksonville in early June. The Marlins' 9.83 tNERD is buoyed by a young, cheap roster and a hot streak of racing around the bases with Otto Lopez, currently drawing trade buzz, leading the majors in batting average. Philadelphia, meanwhile, is scuffling and has fallen further back in the NL East. Not a great pitching matchup on paper, but Luzardo alone makes it worth a look.

Chicago Cubs @ St. Louis Cardinals, 4:45p

Summary

Chicago's fielding and offense make this one worth a look, and the Cardinals' season is dangling by a thread, which adds some drama even if St. Louis isn't the flashier side. The Cubs (61-46) have won seven of ten, riding a wild-card push and coming off back-to-back blowouts of St. Louis, including a 10-2 win that saw them overpower the Cardinals offensively for the second straight game, while St. Louis has lost eight of their last ten and as a result, their season is on life support. Chicago's tNERD of 8.74 is well above the historic 75th percentile, propped up by standout fielding and batting runs, though a shaky bullpen (-1.19) is a real weak spot. St. Louis's 6.30 is respectable too, boosted by a young, cheap roster that scores well on the age and payroll components. On the mound, Dustin May (6.44 pNERD) brings mid-90s-plus velocity and a strong xFIP-, and reports have him finding another gear recently, with his strikeout rate climbing over his last few starts. Matthew Boyd (5.28 pNERD) is steadier than flashy, with solid command peripherals. Combined gNERD of 13.38 sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, making this one of the more watchable options.

Baltimore Orioles @ Detroit Tigers, 10:10a

Summary

Great, this is exactly what I needed - a dramatic result. Let me write the summary now.

Tarik Skubal's likely farewell start in a Tigers uniform turned into an instant classic, and this recap captures why the whole night was must-watch. With the Aug. 3 trade deadline looming and Detroit lingering under .500, this was billed as Skubal's most anticipated outing—possibly his final start as a Detroit Tiger, as the trade deadline draws closer and the Tigers remain mired in the playoff race. He delivered a milestone moment, too: Skubal got his first standing ovation when he struck out leadoff hitter Taylor Ward on a 3-2 changeup to record his 1,000th career strikeout, then tipped his cap to the fans. But the story didn't end there—Skubal was taking a 7-0 shutout into the seventh inning against Baltimore, but then the Orioles rallied from a 7-0 deficit to beat Detroit 10-9 in 12 innings.

The NERD numbers back up the hype: this game's 13.37 gNERD sits comfortably above the historic average of 10.11, and well above today's slate average too. Skubal's 12.86 pNERD is elite—driven by a filthy 58 xFIP-, top-shelf swinging-strike and strike rates, and mid-90s-plus velocity—while Trevor Rogers is merely average opposite him. Both bullpens and lineups are middling by tNERD, but none of that matters once Skubal starts humming; just don't expect a shutout given how the last meeting between these two clubs went.

Atlanta Braves @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

Chris Sale is worth clearing your schedule for, and the Mets' late-inning meltdowns make this Braves-Mets finale unexpectedly watchable too. This is the highest gNERD of the day, and it's not close — a 12.97 that sits comfortably above the historic 75th percentile and right in line with today's slate average of 10.97.

Sale is the headline: at 37, he's carrying a 192 ERA+, his best mark since 2018, and comes in carrying a 2.19 ERA and 134 strikeouts across 111.0 innings. His pNERD of 9.03 is driven by elite xFIP- and swinging-strike numbers, though his deliberate pace docks him slightly. Christian Scott, the Mets' Tommy-John-surgery-recovering righthander, is a solid complement with a 5.87 pNERD, even though he's coming off his shortest outing since his season debut, lasting just 3 2/3 innings against Milwaukee. He's also struggled specifically against Atlanta, going 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA in two starts against the Braves.

The Mets' offense is genuinely unpredictable — Francisco Lindor hit two of the Mets' four homers in a 14-3 romp over the Braves in the series opener — while Atlanta's bullpen has been overworked, giving extra intrigue to how long Sale can go. Both team tNERDs sit in solid-average territory, but the pitching matchup carries this one comfortably above the pack.

Arizona Diamondbacks @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 9:35a

Summary

A near must-watch: a rookie-level pNERD gap between two hot pitchers, wrapped in a wild-card dogfight between two teams separated by a single game. Jared Jones, working back from Tommy John surgery, has been the story of Pittsburgh's July — he's allowed only three earned runs in 21 innings while going 1-0 over his past four starts, striking out 28 and walking only four batters, and his 98.6 mph average velocity and gaudy xFIP- of 79 back up the eye test, driving a 10.53 pNERD that's comfortably above today's average. Eduardo Rodriguez counters with a much shakier peripheral profile (2.36 pNERD, thin strikeout stuff), even though he's one of the league's hottest pitchers this year, having made his first All-Star team in his 11-year career — a classic results-versus-process mismatch. The Pirates' 7.34 tNERD, built on strong batting and baserunning, edges Arizona's more defense-and-luck-driven 4.97 mark. Layer on the stakes — the two teams are back where they started after splitting two extra-inning games, with Arizona holding a one-game edge in the wild-card race entering the finale — and the 12.60 gNERD, comfortably above the historical average, feels earned.

Milwaukee Brewers @ San Francisco Giants, 12:45p

Summary

Good news for the Brewers, bad news for anyone hoping for a pitcher's duel: this one leans on Milwaukee's excellent roster more than anything Logan Webb's opponent brings to the mound. The headline storyline is Thomas Pannone, a left-hander getting a surprise spot start after Milwaukee optioned Garrett Stallings and bumped Shane Drohan back a turn — Pannone returns to the major leagues after completing his recovery from a left forearm flexor tendon tear that sidelined him throughout the 2025 season, and it's just his second big-league appearance since 2023, so there's zero pNERD data to lean on and plenty of uncertainty. Webb, by contrast, has actually been struggling in July as he enters today with a 7.54 ERA, striking out just 13 batters over 22.2 innings, though his underlying xFIP- of 89 still earns him a solid 5.66 pNERD and he's owned this matchup before, having shut them out on one hit over seven innings in a 1-0 win at Milwaukee on June 3. The real draw is Milwaukee's tNERD of 8.81 — young, athletic, deep bullpen — against a slightly unlucky Giants club that's actually outperforming its peripherals. At 11.95, this gNERD sits comfortably above the historic average and squarely in today's middle tier.

Atlanta Braves @ New York Mets, 10:10a

Summary

A feel-good comeback story headlines this one more than the pitching stat lines do. AJ Smith-Shawver takes the mound for the first time since tearing his UCL in May 2025, and his final rehab tune-up—his fastball sat at 97.5 mph in his final rehab start, and the right-hander posted a 1.53 ERA across five Minor League outings—suggests the stuff is back even if the pitch count (built up to just 86) means a quick hook is likely. Since he's making his season debut, there's simply no data to grade him on, so his 0.00 pNERD is more "unknown quantity" than "bad pitcher." Across from him, Sean Manaea has been rough lately—posting a 5.08 FIP across his last two appearances while allowing 1.69 HR/9—though his 5.49 pNERD gets a boost from a lively strike rate and slow pace. This is the makeup half of a doubleheader after Monday's 14-3 Mets rout, so revenge is on the docket for Atlanta. The Braves' 6.12 tNERD (strong bullpen, solid barrel rate) edges the Mets' 4.92, and a 10.76 gNERD lands right around the historical middle—watchable mostly for the human-interest angle rather than the raw ledger.

Summary

This one is a tick below average on the gNERD scale—today's slate ranges from 5.82 to 16.47, and 8.46 sits closer to the low end, mostly because both teams' tNERD marks (2.62 for Kansas City, 2.87 for Minnesota) are well under the historical mean of 5.23, dragged down by shaky bullpens and, for the Twins, middling fielding.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ San Francisco Giants, 6:45p

Summary

Kansas City Royals @ Minnesota Twins, 4:40p

Summary

Good enough info gathered. Let me write the summary.

This one's mostly about watching a good pitcher face a fading team, not a marquee showdown between contenders. Taj Bradley has quietly turned into one of the better arms in the league this July, and the Royals' anemic bullpen and playoff-caliber Twins offense make this a lopsided watch on paper — though Lugo has his own case to make.

Hoping to bolster the Twins' postseason chances, Taj Bradley (9-4, 3.69 ERA) will look to stamp a solid July, and the 25-year-old is 3-1 with a 2.90 ERA in his last five starts, throwing seven innings of one-run, two-hit ball against Cleveland in his last outing. His 97 mph velocity and youth show up plainly in his 6.55 pNERD, comfortably above today's 5.78 average. Lugo, meanwhile, is quietly making a case as a deadline chip: in two post-All-Star break starts, Lugo has made himself into an interesting trade candidate, allowing just four combined earned runs in 13 innings, including a win against San Francisco. His pNERD (3.68) undersells that recent stretch given his pedestrian velocity and lackluster whiff rate, but he historically hasn't fared well against Minnesota (1-3 with a 5.24 ERA in 10 career appearances against the Twins). Team-wise, both sides sit at a middling 2.64 tNERD — Kansas City's brutal bullpen drags it down, Minnesota's shaky defense and baserunning do the same — putting the 7.76 gNERD below both the historic and today's averages. Watch for the pitching, not the standings race.

Philadelphia Phillies @ Miami Marlins, 3:40p

Summary

Zack Wheeler is quietly having one of the better seasons in baseball and Miami is in full collapse mode—that combination makes this worth your evening. The Marlins have dropped 12 straight games, a franchise record, and have yet to win since the All-Star break. Wheeler counters that misery by walking in with a sparkling 10-2 record and a 2.16 ERA, backed by an xFIP- of just 65 and elite swinging-strike rate that push his pNERD to 9.09, comfortably above today's average. Tyler Phillips is a serviceable but unspectacular foil — decent velocity, shaky command, a 110 xFIP- — giving this matchup a real talent gap on the mound, even if the raw box score (2-5, 3.52 ERA) undersells how rough his peripherals have been. On the offensive side, Philadelphia's lineup can erupt (Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber's 33 homers lead the way) though the Phillies own tNERD is middling due to underwhelming batting runs. Miami, despite the losing streak, posts a strong 9.62 tNERD thanks to speed, a young roster, and bad luck that suggests better days ahead — Otto Lopez's .328 average and Xavier Edwards' on-base ability keep the bottom-feeder lineup from being a total non-factor. With a 14.03 gNERD, this sits near the top of today's slate and comfortably above the historical average.

Neither team is going anywhere this year, but this one at least has two starters currently pitching better than their peripherals suggest and a bit of narrative texture to spice up a Monday matchup between fourth-place clubs. Chicago Cubs @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 10:35a

Summary

A dominant Ashcraft strikeout arm meets a Cubs offense riding a 31-run scoring binge, making this the day's most watchable matchup on paper. At 15.67, today's gNERD sits well above both the historic average (10.11) and today's slate average (11.32), and it's driven mostly by a lopsided pitching matchup: Braxton Ashcraft's 11.58 pNERD (elite xFIP-, 97 mph heat, brisk pace) dwarfs Jameson Taillon's modest 3.97. That said, Ashcraft's last outing saw him give up seven earned runs in three innings against the Yankees, so buyer beware on recent form even as his skills grade out well. The Pirates enter having Pittsburgh hosting the Cubs while riding a three-game losing skid and are trying to avoid a series sweep. Both offenses carry real juice—Chicago's tNERD (8.49) and Pittsburgh's (7.30) both rank comfortably above the historic 75th percentile—with Pete Crow-Armstrong pacing Chicago in OBP (.390) and slugging (.544) and Bryan Reynolds anchoring Pittsburgh. Add in Taillon's history as a former Pirate first-round product returning to PNC Park, and there's enough juice here to make this the pick of the day.

Colorado Rockies @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski is must-watch theater against a Rockies team that has no business being in this ballpark, and the numbers back that up as strongly as anything on today's slate. Misiorowski, the 24-year-old flamethrower who's become a genuine Cy Young conversation piece, leads the majors with 173 strikeouts and in ERA, and he consistently hits 100 mph or more on the radar gun. His pNERD of 15.00 is essentially maxed out, driven by elite whiff rates, a microscopic xFIP-, and velocity that sits near the top of the league — this is as close to appointment viewing as a start gets. Opposite him, Kyle Freeland has been scuffling, having lost his last two decisions, allowing four runs over six innings in both outings, though his pNERD of 5.37 is respectable thanks to strong control and some rough luck. The Brewers' 8.87 tNERD (driven by baserunning, bullpen depth, and a young, boosted lineup) dwarfs Colorado's league-worst 1.41, with Milwaukee's rookies Cooper Pratt and Luis Lara instrumental in Saturday night's 8-5 Milwaukee win. At 15.32, this gNERD ranks near the top of both today's games and the historical distribution — mostly on the strength of one dominant arm.

New York Yankees @ Philadelphia Phillies, 4:20p

Summary

I've got enough to write a solid summary now.

Watch this one for Sánchez alone — a legitimate Cy Young-caliber arm against a Yankees lineup that leads baseball in team ERA, with the Phillies trying to snap a home skid. Cristopher Sánchez brings a 10.21 pNERD, driven by an absurd 61 xFIP-, elite swinging-strike rate, and plus velocity — this is a top-shelf starter having a genuinely dominant season. This is his 22nd start of the season, and the 29-year-old carries a 2.65 ERA with a 6.04 strikeout-to-walk ratio. That said, July has been rough for him, with a 7.47 ERA and 1.98 WHIP across 16 innings, plus a jump in barrel rate — worth watching whether he's settling back in. Opposite him, Will Warren (4.33 pNERD) is a more pedestrian arm, prone to traffic on the bases, though he's shown flashes of getting outs when it matters. The Yankees' 8.54 tNERD is the headline offensive story here — strong barrel rates, baserunning, and bullpen — while Philadelphia's 5.34 leans more on baserunning and pen depth than its middling bat. Philadelphia sits at 27-27 at home and 38-5 when scoring five-plus runs, so a quiet Phillies bat could make this lopsided fast. At 14.21 gNERD, this ranks comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — a good pick.

Two of the best right-handed arms in the league face off in Texas, with the AL West standings actually meaning something for once—well worth clearing the schedule for this one.

Seattle rolls into Globe Life Field having lost the first two of this four-game set and slipped to third in the division, while Texas has grabbed early control of the series behind a resurgent offense. The first-place Rangers have won the first two games in the four-game series that will continue when ace right-handers Logan Gilbert of Seattle and Jacob deGrom of Texas oppose each other for the third time this season. deGrom, now 38, remains a marvel of late-career excellence—his pNERD of 10.87 is driven by elite strikeout stuff and command, backed by the lowest career WHIP and second-lowest ERA of any starting pitcher in the live-ball era among those with at least 1000 innings. Miami's on a five-game home skid that has them "one loss to Padres away from ugly franchise mark," a stunning reversal after they'd gone 26-8 from June 1 to July 9, the best in baseball. Detail

Chicago Cubs @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

A rare treat: this is the day's best watch, headlined by a legit ace-versus-ace pitching duel with actual stakes attached. Paul Skenes brings a 10.25 pNERD—tops among today's slate—built on elite xFIP- and a 96.9 mph heater, and even though his surface numbers have wobbled lately (a 4.93 ERA in his last seven starts, "nearly a run and a half higher than his three-year career mark"), the underlying stuff still grades out excellent. Across from him, Shota Imanaga (5.93 pNERD) has quietly caught fire, posting a 1.62 ERA over three July starts and threw seven scoreless innings last time out. Both clubs bring real thump: the Cubs' 8.29 tNERD leans on standout fielding and batting runs, while Pittsburgh's 7.44 mixes strong baserunning with a payroll-underdog appeal. The two teams are tied 4-4 in the season series, and with both teams carrying genuine postseason ambitions, the Cubs at 58-45 clinging to a wild-card spot and Pittsburgh right on the edge of that conversation, there's context to match the talent. At 15.96, the gNERD score sits well above both the historic 95th percentile (14.76) and today's average (11.06)—about as good as it gets.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ New York Mets, 4:15p

Summary

Good pitchers' duel — the Dodgers' ace against the Mets' emerging rookie phenom, and both are dealing right now. Yamamoto and McLean actually met once before this season in a tight April duel, and this rematch has real juice: Yamamoto is coming off a pedestrian 3.60 ERA as recently as May 12 before pitching to a 2.20 mark over 10 starts, including his last outing, a complete-game two-run performance. McLean, meanwhile, has been quietly dominant, with a 0.75 ERA over his last four starts, including an active streak of 17 consecutive innings without an earned run, built on a new approach of lasting at least six innings in six straight starts by peppering the strike zone with four-seamers and sinkers early in counts rather than his breaking stuff. Both pitchers grade out well above average here — McLean edges Yamamoto slightly thanks to youth and a quicker pace, and their near-identical xFIP- marks confirm this isn't just ERA magic. The Dodgers bring by far the day's best offense, riding a 65-38 record, while the Mets counter with a middling lineup — but that pitching matchup alone makes this one of the stronger watches on the board, well above both the historical and today's average gNERD marks.

San Diego Padres @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

A rare high-end matinee: young flamethrower Eury Pérez against a lineup that's finally waking up, in a game that ranks near the top of both today's slate and the season overall. This one carries a gNERD of 14.31, comfortably above the historic median and near the upper end of today's games, driven almost entirely by two well-rounded, entertaining teams rather than a marquee pitching duel. Pérez is the story here — the 23-year-old is carrying a 1.14 ERA over his past seven starts, most recently allowing one hit over six shutout innings against Milwaukee, and his 98 mph heat and elite swinging-strike rate back up a strong 7.91 pNERD. Sears, by contrast, sits at a modest 1.99 pNERD — he's bounced back in July with a 2.51 ERA in three starts after a rough start to his Padres tenure, but the peripherals (poor strike-throwing, plodding pace) suggest he's more innings-eater than headliner. Where this game earns its keep is on the position-player side: both clubs grade out near 9.5 tNERD, with Miami's young, cheap, feisty roster and San Diego's baserunning/bullpen/fielding combo giving this the look of two frisky underdogs — San Diego's lineup has averaged 6.71 runs per game since the break, including a 19-run outburst, despite going just 2-5 over that span. Worth tuning in for the contrast alone.

Seattle Mariners @ Texas Rangers, 4:15p

Summary

I have enough information from the searches already gathered to write a solid, specific summary.

Two of the best pitchers in baseball this year face off in a game that means real division standings, not just style points. Bryan Woo and Nathan Eovaldi both grade out among the more effective starters, and the Rangers-Mariners series carries genuine stakes in a scrambled AL West race.

This is a rematch of an ongoing AL West battle where the AL West has been wide open all season, with the Rangers clinging to a half-game lead in first place while the Mariners are eager to re-establish their position as division favorites. Seattle arrives in a funk — still searching for answers after a rough loss to the Reds, with the trade deadline approaching and this series carrying real weight on how the team approaches upgrading the roster — while the Rangers lead the season series 4-2, meaning anything more than a split would give them the tiebreaker if the race comes down to September.

The pitching is the real draw. Eovaldi's xFIP- of 79 and elite swinging-strike rate power a pNERD near 8.4, while Woo backs him with plus velocity and command for a 7.66 mark — both well above today's average of 5.52 and comfortably in the upper quartile of the historic range. Texas's tNERD (6.06) outpaces Seattle's shaky, error-prone unit (2.69, dragged down by weak fielding and baserunning), though the Rangers' outsized batting luck (+34, one of the highest values you'll see) suggests some regression could be coming. Combined, the 12.38 gNERD sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — a solid, quietly compelling pitchers' duel wrapped in postseason-race tension.

Summary

A solid mid-tier matchup with a pitching subplot worth tuning into: Bryce Elder trying to shake off a rough stretch against Baltimore's quietly excellent rookie-ish righty. Atlanta arrives with the better all-around roster (tNERD 6.78 vs. 4.79), fueled by a strong bullpen and barrel-rate advantage, while Baltimore's lineup and pen are merely adequate. Elder carries a 4.06 ERA and 1.23 WHIP over 19 starts, but across his past three outings owns a bloated 6.43 ERA and has allowed a .283 batting average against — though a report suggests he was dealing with fatigue and had a better start coming out of the All-Star break, so there's a track-record-versus-recent-blip storyline here. Young, meanwhile, is 8-2 with a 3.25 ERA, and 3-0 across his past five starts, lasting seven innings in each of his past two, though his underlying xFIP- suggests he's overachieving. Elder's excellent pace and youth push his pNERD to a respectable 5.27; Young trails at 3.56. Overall gNERD of 10.20 sits almost exactly at the historical median — a perfectly fine, unspectacular Saturday option rather than a must-watch.

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

New York Yankees @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:45p

Summary

Highest gNERD score of the day, and two of the game's marquee arms make it easy to justify skipping the remote control. This is genuinely the marquee pitching matchup of this Yankees-Phillies series, and it's built on two pitchers having standout seasons rather than reputation alone.

Schlittler currently sits as the odds-on favorite to win the AL Cy Young award and carries a 2.20 ERA into action, having fanned 145 batters in 123.0 innings, and the underlying numbers back it up — his xFIP- and swinging-strike rates both grade elite, with plus-97 mph heat to match. entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Minnesota Twins @ Cleveland Guardians, 10:10a

Summary

Cleveland's had this Twins series circled all week, and the last game of a four-game set arrives with the Guardians already up 2-1 and both starters carrying real swing-and-miss stuff. Gavin Williams headlines the day: his 11.10 pNERD is comfortably above today's average and sits in rare territory historically, powered by a strong xFIP (74, well better than league average) and elite strikeout/whiff numbers. Williams owns a 2.39 xFIP over the last 30 days, which does not align with his 4.70 ERA, and this looks like a good matchup for the numbers to finally catch up. That underperformance shows up in his positive luck component, suggesting better results than his ERA lately would indicate. Taj Bradley isn't chopped liver either, with a 6.87 pNERD boosted by mid-90s-plus velocity, though Bradley holds a clear edge against this specific opponent, owning a 1.54 ERA in four career starts versus the Guardians, including a 10-strikeout outing over seven innings on July 7. On the team side, Cleveland's 7.73 tNERD (aided by a young, inexpensive roster and a strong bullpen) dwarfs Minnesota's underwhelming 2.37, and Cleveland has outscored Minnesota 28-12 across the first three games of this series. With a gNERD of 14.03 - well above both the historical and today's averages - this is one of the more watchable matchups on the board, thanks almost entirely to the pitching.

Kansas City Royals @ Detroit Tigers, 3:40p

Summary

Melton's on a roll, Dobnak's ERA is lying to you, and this is a Comerica Park pitchers' park special that's more watchable for the arms than the lineups. Troy Melton, the sport's most under-the-radar strikeout artist of the moment, carries a genuinely strong pNERD of 7.89, boosted by mid-90s velocity, a quick pace, and youth on his side.

Melton is genuinely hot, allowing one earned run in 17 1/3 innings with 25 strikeouts across three July starts. His xFIP- backs it up — this isn't just a hot streak, it's real stuff. Dobnak, on the other hand, gets a pNERD of 0 simply because we lack the data to grade him properly; he's making his fourth appearance of the season and second start since being called up from Triple-A, and early returns (a shiny ERA propped up by sequencing luck, not process) suggest regression looms.

Team-wise, neither club brings much thump — Detroit's tNERD of 4.78 and Kansas City's 2.81 both sit below average, dragged down by a genuinely brutal Royals bullpen (their bullpen-runs component is one of the worst you'll see). Both teams carry modest positive luck, meaning slight over-performance may be more sustainable than usual, but nothing dramatic. With a gNERD of 10.24, this lands almost exactly at today's slate average — watch it for Melton's arm, not for the lineups.

Detail

New York Mets @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Good. The Brewers lead the NL Central at 63-37/38, the best record in the National League, while the Mets sit well below .500 on the road. Both starters are having strong seasons, with Henderson working on a limited pitch/innings count and Scott coming off dominant back-to-back starts.

The Brewers' best-in-the-NL record meets a Mets club playing out the string, but the pitching matchup makes this worth a look anyway. Milwaukee enters at the National League Central at 63-37, the best record in the senior circuit, while New York limps in having gone 22-31 in road games and 43-59 overall. That imbalance shows up in the tNERD gap—Brewers 8.34 to the Mets' 4.23—Milwaukee's young, cheap, athletic roster (lowest average age, strong baserunning and bullpen marks) contrasting with a Mets team whose big-money roster hasn't hit or run the bases well this year. The pitching is the real draw. Logan Henderson, just 24, has been outstanding: a 2.45 ERA, 2.84 FIP, and 71 strikeouts over 58 2/3 innings across his brief career, and his 8.85 pNERD ranks near the top of today's slate. Christian Scott isn't far behind, riding 10 2/3 innings with no runs allowed and 12 strikeouts against the Royals and Phillies in his last two outings. Both are first-time opponents for each other, adding a little novelty. At 13.69, the gNERD comfortably clears today's average of 10.44, making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board despite the standings gap.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ New York Yankees, 10:05a

Summary

Good storylines found. Now let me write the summary.

Cole against his old team is the headline, and the underlying numbers back it up as a genuinely solid watch. Gerrit Cole draws Pittsburgh — the franchise that drafted him first overall 15 years ago — in the opener of a rain-forced doubleheader, and he's been mostly excellent since returning from last spring's Tommy John surgery. His 6.06 pNERD is comfortably above average, driven by strong strike-throwing and velocity that's actually ticked up to 96.8 mph; the only blemish has been a recent tendency to serve up homers, with eight home runs allowed already, a number Cole and the Yankees are watching closely. Mitch Keller is more of a middling stopgap here (3.30 pNERD), held back by unremarkable swing-and-miss stuff, though positive pitching luck suggests his results have actually undersold his stuff. Where this game earns its 13.06 gNERD — comfortably above both the historical average and today's slate — is the lineups: both Pittsburgh and New York rank near the top of the league in barrel rate and baserunning value, and the Yankees' 8.86 tNERD is buoyed by strong bullpen and contact-quality metrics. A well-rounded, above-average game worth carving out time for.

Boston has won 14 straight and sits one victory from tying the franchise record for consecutive wins, a run that stands as the longest in Major League Baseball this season and the longest in the majors since the Brewers won 14 in a row last August. Lefty Jake Bennett draws the assignment, and it's uncharted territory for both sides since Bennett is facing the Orioles for the first time. His pNERD of 7.02 is legitimately strong, built on plus strike-throwing and a tidy pace, and at 25 he's exactly the kind of prospect worth watching build a track record in real time. Dean Kremer counters with a 6.31 pNERD boosted heavily by good fortune — his ERA-beating xFIP gap accounts for most of his score, so some regression could be lurking. Boston's tNERD (6.27) edges Baltimore's (4.74), powered by strong fielding and bullpen work, while the Orioles counter with modest pop and Baltimore's own quieter three-city-comparable run of form. At 12.17, the gNERD sits comfortably above the historical average and this season's daily average, making it a solidly above-average watch, streak drama included.

San Diego Padres @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Two flawed-but-scrappy contenders meet in a game that's more watchable for its randomness than its star power. Atlanta, banged up all year, enters having outscored opponents while riding a top-three NL bullpen and a 3.61 team ERA, but injuries have gutted the roster — Ronald Acuña Jr., Spencer Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach, and Sean Murphy are all out, and Martín Pérez himself has been shuttling on and off the 15-day IL with a forearm issue, so his return to the mound carries its own intrigue.
